error.rateStuck: the device didn't switch to {rate} kHz (still at {current} kHz)

error.dopRefused: {device} can't take DoP for {dsd} (it needs {rate} kHz, 24 bits, exclusive mode)

test.title: Channel check
test.subtitle: First a low tone in the left ear, then a high one in the right
display.label: Display
step.pcmToDsdNative5: PCM → {dsd} (5th-order modulator), native DSD at {rate} MHz
step.pcmToDsdNative7: PCM → {dsd} (7th-order modulator), native DSD at {rate} MHz
step.downmix: {from} mixed down to {to}, {db} dB so it never clips
step.headroomPending: {db} dB of headroom against clipping (while the track loads)
verdict.empty: Add music to the queue and the signal path to your headphones will appear here.
verdict.test: First a low tone in the left ear, then a high one in the right. If it's the other way round, the channels are swapped.
verdict.dop: The DAC gets the file's DSD stream bit for bit, packed as DoP.
verdict.native: The DAC gets the file's DSD stream bit for bit, natively (no DoP).
verdict.iosVolume: The DAC gets the file's samples, but the iPhone volume is below maximum, so iOS may recalculate them. For bit-perfect playback, set the iPhone volume to maximum and adjust the volume on the DAC.
verdict.bitPerfect: The DAC gets exactly the samples stored in the file.
verdict.network: The network player gets exactly the samples stored in the file.
verdict.lossy: The file is lossy-compressed. The DAC gets the decoded signal unchanged.
verdict.clip: The signal hits 0 dBFS: the equalizer raises the level too much.
dsd.exclusive: DoP works only in exclusive mode
dsd.exclusiveNative: native DSD works only in exclusive mode
dsd.volume: for DoP the iPhone volume must be at maximum; adjust the volume on the DAC
dsd.dsp: the equalizer and crossfeed work on PCM
dsd.rate: {device} doesn't run at {rate} kHz, which DoP {dsd} needs
dsd.rateNativeDop: {device} doesn't take {dsd} natively, nor run at {rate} kHz, which DoP needs
dsd.channels: the file has more channels ({n}) than the device, and DoP can't mix them down
dsd.channelsNative: the file has more channels ({n}) than the device, and native DSD can't mix them down
dsdOutNote.device: DoP is not switched on for this device
dsdOutNote.volume: the iPhone volume is below maximum
dsdOutNote.network: a network player doesn't take DSD
dsdOutNote.rate: {device} doesn't take DoP ({rate} kHz, 24 bits needed)
enh.perDevice: Each output has its own processing. A new one starts without any.
enh.upsamplingHelp: Resamples the track to the highest rate of the same family that the DAC accepts ({a} → {b}, 48 → 384).
enh.filter.standardHelp: Short, linear phase, about 100 dB of stopband attenuation.
enh.filter.linearHelp: A sharp cut right at the recording's limit. Ringing is split evenly before and after a transient.
enh.filter.minimumHelp: The same cut, with all the ringing after the transient.
enh.filter.apodizingHelp: Cuts slightly below the limit and removes the ringing a mastering filter left. Short; rings only after the transient.
enh.lengthHelp: A longer filter makes the transition at the limit narrower: {a} Hz, or {b} Hz, for a {rate} kHz recording. Attenuation is the same, 150 dB.
enh.lengthAhead: Linear phase at this length reads 6 seconds of music ahead, so tracks from streaming start a little later.
enh.stepShorter: The processor could not keep up: the filter length was reduced to {length}.
enh.stepStandard: The processor could not keep up: the standard filter is on.
enh.dsdHelp: Turns PCM into a one-bit DSD stream and sends it to the DAC natively or as DoP. This is processing: the sound is no longer bit-perfect. DSD files play as they are.
enh.dsdNeeds: Needs exclusive mode, and a DAC that takes DSD natively or has DoP switched on.
enh.dsdUpsampling: While DSD output is on, the track is upsampled to the DSD rate, not the one chosen here. The filter still applies.
enh.modulator.7Help: Less noise in the audible band, more work for the processor. Signal-to-noise up to 20 kHz: {db} dB.
enh.modulator.5Help: Lighter on the processor. Signal-to-noise up to 20 kHz: {db} dB.
enh.dsdStepRate: The processor could not keep up: output lowered to {dsd}.
enh.dsdStepOrder: The processor could not keep up: switched to the 5th-order modulator.
enh.dsdStepOff: The processor could not keep up: DSD output turned off.
enh.dsdLimited: This device takes no more than {dsd} over DoP.
enh.dsdLimitedNative: This device takes no more than {dsd} natively.
enh.eqHelp: Parametric and graphic EQ with presets per output, linear phase, convolution and import from AutoEQ, Equalizer APO, Wavelet and REW.
enh.crossfeedHelp: Mixes a softer copy of the opposite channel into each ear, as when you listen to speakers. Removes the “sound inside your head” feeling on recordings with hard-panned stereo.
enh.headroomHelp: After decoding, MP3 peaks often go past 0 dBFS, and loud passages crackle. The player measures the overshoot across the whole track and lowers the level by exactly that much, usually less than 1 dB.
enh.restoreHelp: Finds where the codec cut off the highs (16–19 kHz for 128–256 kbps MP3) and rebuilds the octave above from the harmonics of the band below. It's a plausible reconstruction, not a return of what was lost. Files cut off above 20 kHz are left alone.
enh.losslessNote: Lossless files aren't affected by these settings; they play as before.
enh.footerLossy: Lossless files go to the DAC bit-perfect, MP3 and AAC with corrections.
enh.footerPure: No processing is on: the signal goes to the DAC bit-perfect.
enh.footerOn: Bit-perfect is off because of: {what}. With that off, lossless files go to the DAC untouched again.
dev.networkSearching: Looking for Sonos, WiiM, Bluesound, Chromecast and other UPnP/DLNA and Google Cast players on this network…
dev.networkHelp: The music goes to the player over your network as FLAC, sample for sample. For bit-perfect sound, keep the player's own EQ and volume leveling off.
dev.iosNote: iPhone plays through one output: whichever is connected now. Connect a DAC over USB-C and the sound goes to it at the file's sample rate. Other apps go quiet meanwhile.
dev.androidExclusiveHelp: Android 14 and later hand the USB DAC over to the player entirely: no Android mixer, no system volume, and the DAC's rate follows each track. Adjust the volume on the DAC.
dev.exclusiveHelp: Other apps can't mix in their sound, and the DAC's rate follows each track.
dev.exclusiveAlways: ASIO always has the DAC to itself.
dev.dopHelp: DSD files go to {device} as they are, up to DSD{max}. Turn this on only if the DAC supports DoP: otherwise you'll hear quiet noise instead of music. When it's off, DSD is converted to PCM. DSD output in Enhancers needs it too.
dev.nativeDsd: Native DSD up to DSD{max}: DSD files go to {device} as they are, no DoP needed.
dev.dopHelpNative: Only for DoP, at rates {device} doesn't take natively (up to DSD{max}). Turn this on only if the DAC supports DoP: otherwise you'll hear quiet noise instead of music.
dev.testHelp: First a low tone on the left, then a high one on the right.
dev.driverSettingsHelp: Opens the driver's own window: buffer size and more.
dev.speaker: Speaker
lib.label: Library
lib.sort.title: by title
lib.iosHelp: The library is the app's folder: Files → On My iPhone → BitSpring. Copy albums there with the Files app or with Finder on a Mac (iPhone → Files), or add files here.
lib.ownFolderHelp: for DSD files (DSF, DFF), which Android hides from apps in other folders: {path}
lib.hideFolderAsk: Skip the folder “{name}” with everything in it?
lib.iosOnlyFolder: iPhone gives an app only its own folder, so there are no other folders to choose.
lib.skipHelp: A skipped folder stays out of the library with everything inside it: handy for ringtones, call recordings or podcasts. Playlists keep their tracks.
lib.skipNone: No folders with music in here.

lib.failed.other: {n} files couldn't be read: damaged or in an unsupported format.

lib.emptyAndroid: Copy albums to the Music folder in the phone's internal storage, over USB from a computer or with a file manager, then tap “Rescan”. If the app asked for access to music, allow it.
lib.emptyIos: Copy albums to Files → On My iPhone → BitSpring (or from a Mac with Finder: iPhone → Files → BitSpring) and the library will find them by itself. Or add files from here.
lib.emptyDesktop: Choose a folder with music, such as Music in your home folder or an external drive. The files stay where they are: the app only reads tags and artwork.

remote.denied: This address no longer works. Open the one shown in BitSpring on the computer: the phone icon at the top of the window.
remote.offline: No connection to BitSpring. Is it running on the computer, and is this phone on the same network?

pl.pasteHintLocal: One track per line: “Artist — Title” or a file path. The contents of a playlist file or a table (Exportify, TuneMyMusic, an Apple Music export) work too.

sp.empty: No tracks in the library match these rules.

stream.needPlan: You need a plan with lossless.
stream.needPlanQobuz: You need a plan with lossless (Studio or Sublime).
stream.unofficialWeb: {service} gives independent players no official access to full tracks, so the player talks to the service the way its own web player does, like the open-source players Strawberry and Mopidy. The service may shut that access down. Encrypted streams are not played.
stream.unofficialAndroid: {service} gives independent players no official access to full tracks, so the player talks to the service the way its own Android app does, like the open-source players Strawberry and Mopidy. The service may shut that access down. Encrypted streams are not played.
stream.note.noLossless: Your Qobuz plan has no lossless: you'll get MP3 only.
stream.saveToMineTitle: A copy in Library → Playlists that you can edit and export
stream.searchHint: Find an artist, album or track on {service}.
stream.noPlaylists: You have no playlists on {service} yet.

stream.savedCopy.other: “{name}” is now in Library → Playlists ({n} tracks).

eq.title: Equalizer
eq.importHelp: Reads Equalizer APO and Peace, AutoEQ (ParametricEQ, GraphicEQ, CSV), Wavelet, REW, EasyEffects and foobar2000 presets.
eq.hpPopular: Popular headphones. Type a model to search the whole AutoEQ catalog.
eq.hpFirst: First {n} of {total}: type more to narrow it down
eq.hpWhich: Measured by several people. The first is usually the most accurate.
eq.hpNoneOffline: Only popular models are here until the full catalog loads.
eq.hpOffline: The full catalog didn't download, so only popular models are listed.
eq.hpCredit: Profiles by AutoEQ (Jaakko Pasanen, MIT licence), from measurements by oratory1990, crinacle, Rtings and others.
eq.pasteHint: Paste the text of an Equalizer APO or AutoEQ preset, for example as copied from autoeq.app.
eq.emptyTitle: Shape the sound to your headphones
eq.emptyText: Start from a template, or bring in a correction someone has measured for your model: AutoEQ, Equalizer APO, Wavelet and REW files all work.
eq.name: Preset name
eq.compareHelp: Plays without the equalizer at the same average loudness, so you judge the tone, not the volume.
eq.comparing: Without the equalizer, at the same loudness. Press Compare again to hear it.
eq.phaseHelp.minimum: Minimum phase, like an analog equalizer: no pre-ringing, and every change is heard at once.
eq.phaseHelp.linear: Linear phase: no phase shift at any frequency. Sharp, deep cuts can pre-ring before transients. Changes are heard after about half a second.
eq.autoHelp: Lowers the level by exactly the highest boost, so the equalizer can never clip.
eq.clipWarn: With this preamp the curve goes above 0 dBFS and loud passages will clip. Turn on Auto or lower the preamp.
eq.noBands: No bands yet. Double-click the graph where you want one, or add one below.
eq.irHelp: A WAV, FLAC or AIFF impulse response, mono or stereo, up to 6 seconds: room correction made in REW, rePhase or Dirac, or a headphone response. It's applied after the equalizer, and its main peak is lined up so the music stays in time.
eq.editorHelp: Drag a point to change its frequency and gain; scroll over it to change Q. Double-click the graph to add a band. With a point focused, the arrow keys move it (Shift for bigger steps), [ and ] change Q, Delete removes it.
eqHint.text: There are ready-made correction profiles for {model}.
upd.title: Updates
upd.restartNote: The app restarts to finish, which stops playback.
upd.androidNote: Android will ask you to confirm the installation.
error.installNotAllowed: allow BitSpring to install apps on the settings screen that just opened, then press Download and install again
tags.note: Tags are written into the files themselves; the audio in them stays exactly as it is.
tags.readOnly: DSD files and tracks of a CUE image can't be edited here.
q.d.genuineFull: The music fills the file's whole frequency range. No sign of conversion.
q.d.genuineHigh: The music reaches {khz} kHz, beyond what a CD can hold.
q.d.genuineFade: The highs fade out gradually from about {khz} kHz, as in many recordings. No sign of conversion.
q.d.upsampled: Nothing above {khz} kHz: this {rate} kHz file was made from a CD-quality one (44.1 or 48 kHz). It sounds the same as that file and only takes more space.
q.d.mirror: Above {khz} kHz there is only a mirror image of the music below it, the trace a simple resampler leaves. This {rate} kHz file was made from a {from} kHz one: it sounds the same and only takes more space.
q.d.fromLossy: Everything above {khz} kHz is cut off sharply, the way MP3 and AAC encoders do it. A lossless copy can't bring back what they removed.
q.d.padded: The lowest 8 bits of every sample are zero: this is 16-bit audio stored in a 24-bit file.
q.d.lossy: MP3, AAC, Vorbis and Opus leave out part of the sound by design, so there's nothing to unmask here.
q.d.dsd: DSD fills the top of its range with noise by design, so this check doesn't apply.
q.d.short: Too short or too quiet to judge.
q.d.wallAmbiguous: The music stops sharply at {khz} kHz. MP3 at its best settings does that, and so do many CD masters.
q.d.gradualLow: Little above {khz} kHz, and the highs fade out gradually instead of stopping. It may be an old recording, or a file made from a CD or 48 kHz master with a gentle filter.
q.note: Checked on this device, from the sound itself. A verdict is a strong hint, not proof.
enh.levelHelp: Brings every track, or every album, to the same loudness (−18 LUFS) with one fixed gain per track; nothing is compressed. Uses the file's ReplayGain tags, or measures the track itself (EBU R128). A boost stops where the track's peak would clip.
enh.peakHelp: Upsampling, the equalizer, convolution and crossfeed rebuild the waveform, and on loud masters it can peak above 0 dBFS between the samples. The player measures the track's true peak and lowers the level by exactly the overshoot, usually less than 1 dB. Does nothing while those are off.
step.level.trackLimited: volume levelled by track, {db} dB (as far as the peak allows)
step.level.albumLimited: volume levelled by album, {db} dB (as far as the peak allows)
step.level.unknown: volume levelling: this track isn't measured yet
crash.title: BitSpring ran into an error last time
crash.sub: A report is saved on this device, and the app sends it nowhere. It has the app version, your system and the place in the code — no file names, paths or tags. Send it yourself if you want to help fix the bug.
settings.fadesHelp: Fades the sound over 10 ms when you pause, seek, stop or change tracks, so it doesn't end in a click.
settings.fadesSignal: A track playing through, and the join between two tracks, are never touched.
settings.crossfadeHelp: The end of a track fades out under the start of the next, where the album changes. An album played through stays gapless, as it was made.
settings.crossfadeSignal: Only the seconds of the overlap are mixed; the rest of each track is untouched. No crossfade for DSD (DoP or native), tracks at different sample rates or network players.
verdict.crossfade: A crossfade is playing: the end of the previous track is mixed into the start of this one.
verdict.crossfadeAfter: Once it is over, the DAC gets exactly the samples stored in the file again.
settings.asioLicence: This Windows build includes ASIO support under the GNU GPL v3; the source code is on GitHub. ASIO is a registered trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH.
remote.scan: Scan the code with the phone's camera, or open the address in its browser.
remote.where: From now on the code and the address are under the phone icon at the top of the window.
enh.tagsOffer: Measured, not yet in the files' tags: {count}
enh.tagsConfirm: Write the measured loudness into the files' tags (ReplayGain)? Files: {count}. Other players will then level them the same way. The audio stays exactly as it is, and files that already have such tags keep them.
dyn.label: Dynamic range
dyn.help: DR shows how far the peaks stand above the loudest passages: 14 and more is a recording with its dynamics intact, 7 and less is heavily compressed. The loudness range (LRA) is the distance between the quiet and the loud passages. Measured from the sound itself; nothing is changed.
remote.api: The same address lets Home Assistant, a Stream Deck or your own scripts control playback.
abx.title: Blind test (ABX)
abx.processed: the same file with the processing that is switched on
abx.preparing: Getting the two ready: decoding them, lining them up and matching their loudness…
abx.preparingFilters: Getting the two ready: resampling the track with each filter…
abx.identical: These two are the same audio, sample for sample. There is nothing to hear.
abx.unlike: These two don't look like the same recording. The test will run, but it won't tell you much.
abx.how: X is A or B, and the player doesn't say which. Switch between the three as often as you like, then say what X is. Guessing gets about half of the trials right.
abx.heard: You very likely hear a difference.
abx.notHeard: No audible difference shown: this is what guessing looks like. It holds for this music, this equipment and today.
abx.chance: Guessing does at least this well {percent}% of the time.
abx.answers: What X was in each trial
abx.n.processing: B is the file through the equalizer, convolution and crossfeed that are switched on. Upsampling is left out: the DAC would have to switch rates between A and B.
abx.n.rate: Both play at {rate} kHz, so the DAC never switches: {which} was converted from {from} kHz by the player. You compare what the files hold, not how the DAC handles each rate.
abx.n.gain: {which} was turned down by {db} dB, so both are equally loud.
abx.n.level: Both are equally loud as they are.
abx.n.matched: B was brought to the loudness of A. A plays exactly as it is in the file.
abx.n.both: B was brought to the loudness of A, and both were turned down by {db} dB so that B doesn't clip.
abx.n.offset: {which} starts {ms} ms later. The two were lined up to the sample.
abx.n.short: Only the first {time} of the music are compared.
abx.n.fade: Every switch fades for a few milliseconds, the same way whether or not the sound changes.
abx.n.filters: Both versions are this track resampled from {from} to {to} kHz. A: standard filter. B: {filter}.
abx.n.filtersGain: Both are {db} dB quieter so that peaks are not clipped.
abx.compareHelp: Pick another file of the same music, such as the CD edition of a hi-res album, and find out whether you hear the difference.
abx.pick: Another file of the same music
enh.abx: Blind test: do I hear it?
enh.abxHelp: Plays the current track with and without the processing, without saying which is which.
enh.abxFilter: Compare with the standard filter, blind
enh.abxFilterHelp: A blind test: this track resampled to the same rate with each filter. It shows whether you hear a difference.
error.abxChannels: the two files have different channels and can't be compared
error.abxNetwork: a blind test needs a device connected to this computer, not a network player
error.abxNothing: no processing is switched on, so there is nothing to compare
error.abxNotFile: only files can be compared in a blind test
error.abxFilterRate: a long filter runs only from twice the track's rate: {to} Hz is less than twice {from} Hz
error.abxNoFilter: no long upsampling filter is playing this track, so there is nothing to compare it with
rip.ask: This compares the album with other people's rips of the same CD in the CUETools Database (db.cue.tools). Only the lengths of the disc's tracks are sent; the comparison is made on this device.
rip.label: Rip

rip.verified.one: verified. The audio is the same as in {n} other rip of this disc.
rip.verified.other: verified. The audio is the same as in {n} other rips of this disc.

rip.pressing: It is another pressing: its audio is shifted by {n} samples.

rip.partly.one: track {tracks} differs from other people's rips of this disc, the rest match. That track was probably ripped with errors.
rip.partly.other: tracks {tracks} differ from other people's rips of this disc, the rest match. Those tracks were probably ripped with errors.

rip.different.one: it matches nothing in the database, which holds {n} rip of this disc.
rip.different.other: it matches nothing in the database, which holds {n} rips of this disc.

rip.unknown: this disc isn't in the database yet, so there is nothing to compare it with.
rip.unfit.frames: not checked. A track isn't a whole number of CD frames long, so this isn't an untouched CD rip.
rip.unfit.format: not checked. A CD holds 16 bits at 44.1 kHz in stereo.
rip.unfit.length: not checked. This is shorter or longer than a CD can be.
rip.trackHelp: This track's audio differs from other people's rips of the disc
fav.noTracks: No favourite tracks yet. The heart at the end of a track's row makes it one.
fav.noAlbums: No favourite albums yet. Open an album and press the heart beside its title.
settings.ratingsHelp: One to five stars for a track: a column in the track lists, and a row under the title of what plays. Like favourites, ratings stay on this device.
